title: Privacy policy
description: What Story-Tail Adventures collects, how you pay for your trip, and your data rights.

sections.heading: 1. What we collect
paragraphs: Story-Tail Adventures collects contact information, trip details, travel preferences, and travel-document details you choose to share, only to plan and support your trips. The portal has no place to enter a card number, so please don't type one into a message.

We do not sell your information, and we do not share it with marketing third parties. When you use the portal in a web browser, we also count page views without tying them to your name. Section 3 explains who receives what, and why.

If you send Gyasi a note without an account, we keep your name, your email, any phone number you add, your note, and the page or link you wrote from. We keep them so Gyasi can reply and see where people find us. To stop spam, we also keep a scrambled form of your network address for one day. We never email you automatically, and the form refuses card numbers. If you create an account with the same email later, your note joins it. If not, we delete it 24 months after Gyasi closes it.

sections.heading: 2. How you pay for your trip
paragraphs: You pay each supplier directly, on their own secure site. Your advisor adds a pay link to each payment on your trip: the supplier's own payment page, or a Travefy invoice when the supplier doesn't have one. A Travefy invoice passes along supplier costs only. Story-Tail never charges you a planning, consultation or service fee.

Story-Tail never asks for your card number, and the portal has nowhere to keep one. For each payment it keeps the amount, the due date and the pay link, and once your advisor marks it paid, the date, any confirmation number and your advisor's own note. Only your advisor can add or change a pay link, and every change is recorded.

sections.heading: 3. Who we share it with
paragraphs: Trip details and traveler names go to the suppliers who deliver your trip (airlines, resorts, cruise lines, tour operators) and to Inteletravel, the host agency that issues bookings. When you pay a supplier, or a Travefy invoice, you pay them directly on their own site, under their own privacy policy. Our hosting and database providers process data on our behalf under contract.

When you search for hotels, the destination and dates you enter are sent to SerpApi, which returns results from Google Hotels. We do not send your name, your email, or anything else about you — only the search itself.

Hotel photographs on the results page are loaded directly from Google's image servers. That means Google receives your IP address and browser details when a photo loads, as it would for any image on the web. We ask your browser not to tell Google which page you were on.

We keep a record of each hotel search so we can stay inside the search allowance we pay for. The destination and dates are cleared from that record after 30 days; the cached results themselves expire within hours.

If you say yes, the website also counts your visit with Google Analytics, a Google service we reach through Firebase. Nothing is sent to Google until you agree, and you can say no and still use everything. Google Analytics sets its own cookies to tell one visit from another, and it records the page, the site that sent you, your approximate location, and your device and browser. It gets a cleaned-up web address, with ID numbers removed and everything after the “?” dropped except campaign tags, and it never sees the advisor's own pages. We turn off Google's ad features and do not give Google your name or email. You can change your answer any time on the Privacy & data page in your account, or by clearing your browser's site data; turning it off deletes Google's cookies and the visitor code Firebase keeps in your browser. You can read how Google handles this data at policies.google.com/privacy.

sections.heading: 4. Your data rights
paragraphs: You can ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to close your account. Account closure preserves booking and payment records for tax and compliance reasons but anonymizes your personal identifiers. Email us and we will respond within 30 days.

sections.heading: 5. Retention and security
paragraphs: We keep trip and payment records for as long as tax and host-agency rules require, and delete or anonymize the rest when you close your account. Access to sensitive data is logged, and every change to a pay link or a paid payment is recorded.

sections.heading: 6. Contact
paragraphs: Questions about this policy or your data: use the “Message Gyasi” link on any page.

title: Terms of service
description: How the Story-Tail Adventures portal works, what we do and don't charge for, and what you agree to when you use it.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: Story-Tail Adventures is an independent travel advisory business hosted by Inteletravel. Your bookings are issued through Inteletravel and fulfilled by the travel suppliers named on your itinerary. This portal is where you view your trips, message your advisor, and find the link to pay each supplier.

sections.heading: 2. No planning fees
paragraphs: Story-Tail Adventures does not charge planning, consultation or service fees, and our host-agency agreement prohibits it. We earn commission from suppliers when you travel. Prices shown in the portal come from suppliers; supplier terms, deposits and cancellation rules apply to each booking.

sections.heading: 3. Paying suppliers
paragraphs: You pay each supplier directly, through the pay link your advisor adds to each payment on your trip. The link opens the supplier's own payment page, or a Travefy invoice that passes along supplier costs only. Story-Tail never collects or stores card numbers and never charges you a planning or service fee. Each payment is governed by that supplier's terms. Your advisor marks a payment as paid once the supplier confirms it.

sections.heading: 4. Your account
paragraphs: Keep your sign-in details private and let us know if you think someone else has used your account. You are responsible for the accuracy of traveler names, dates of birth and travel-document details you provide; airlines and border authorities require them to match your documents exactly.

sections.heading: 5. Illustrative content
paragraphs: Trip ideas, sample itineraries and starting prices on the public pages are illustrative and change with season, availability and supplier pricing. A quote from your advisor is the only price that binds.

sections.heading: 6. Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms as the portal grows. We will note the date at the top of this page and, for material changes, tell you in the portal or by email.

title: Cookies
description: The small number of cookies and browser storage keys the Story-Tail portal uses, and what each one does.

sections.heading: 1. What we use
paragraphs: The portal uses cookies to keep you signed in and to remember a few preferences. If you allow it, Google Analytics sets a few more to count visits. We do not use advertising cookies.
bullets: Sign-in session cookies (set by our authentication provider, Supabase) so you stay signed in between pages.
A light-or-dark appearance preference, stored in your browser's local storage.
A note that you dismissed the “sign in to save” banner on the search pages, stored in local storage.

Google Analytics cookies (named _ga and _ga_ followed by a code), only if you say yes when the site asks or on the Privacy & data page in your account. They let Google tell one visit from another. Google's ad features are off. Firebase also keeps a visitor code for Google Analytics in your browser's storage. Your answer is kept in your browser's local storage, and turning Google Analytics off deletes these cookies and that code.

sections.heading: 2. Paying suppliers
paragraphs: The portal has no payment form and never asks for a card. When you pay a supplier, you do it on their own site (or on Travefy's, for a Travefy invoice), which may set its own cookies. Those are governed by that site's privacy policy.

sections.heading: 3. Your choices
paragraphs: You can clear cookies and local storage in your browser at any time. Clearing the session cookie signs you out; the portal keeps working for browsing without an account.

title: Accessibility statement
description: How the Story-Tail portal is built to be usable by everyone, what we know still falls short, and how to tell us.

sections.heading: 1. Our commitment
paragraphs: Rest is for everyone, and so is this portal. We build to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA: semantic headings and landmarks, visible focus, keyboard access to every control, text alternatives for images that carry meaning, and layouts that reflow on small screens and at 200% zoom.

sections.heading: 2. What works today
bullets: Every page has one main heading and a skip-to-content link.
Menus, filters and forms work with a keyboard and screen reader; the mobile menu traps focus and closes with Escape.
Light and dark appearance follow your device or your choice.
Legal pages print cleanly in a light palette.

sections.heading: 3. Known limitations
paragraphs: Two brand colour pairs measure below the AA contrast ratio for small text: orange section labels on the cream background, and white text on orange buttons. Both are legible at their sizes but we are working with the designer on adjustments.
Hero photographs carry decorative text overlays; the same information is always available as plain text on the page.

sections.heading: 4. Tell us
paragraphs: If something is hard to use, use the “Message Gyasi” link on any page and describe what happened and what you were trying to do. We will fix what we can quickly and tell you when we have.
